title: Whether jazz will come back and why rock and roll lasted
summary: Francis thought rock would fade but notes people could dance to it, and expects jazz to return to rhythm fundamentals.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Hey, Panama, we were just talking about the arrangers and your part of the 50's and the 60's -- we were saying, in the 30's and the 40's, you and I were all into jazz, and then in the 50's and the 60's, we began the trend with recording rock-and-roll and rhythm-and-blues, and it was the heavily into that end of jazz, sort of.
What was your impression? Did you think jazz was going to come back, as it seems to be doing now? Did you have any idea about that then, or did you hope it or would you have rather had it stay away?
Well, I really didn't expect rock-and-roll to last as long as it has, and I thought sure that eventually the people would go back to jazz.
But then as I thought about it, there was a time where people used to like to dance to jazz, and that was one reason jazz was as popular as it was, especially among black people.

But then, if you remember, when the bebop era came in, the music made a change. Instead of jazz being the music they would listen to, I mean dance to, it became music that they listened to. And so I think -- and maybe I'm wrong -- but I think that's one of the reasons why rock-and-roll was able to have such a foothold because people were able to dance to it. But I really didn't expect it to last as long as it has. (1978--ed.)
Well, this is 1968 -- where do you think jazz stands now?

I have a feeling that it's slowly going back to the basic, which is the foundation, which is rhythm -- that's being put back into it, and drummers are beginning to play their bass drums again, you know? There was a time when all they did was a bass drum was use it to make accents. But not to play time or a beat. And this is between the bass violin and the bass drum, between the two of them, they were the ones that set the pulsation for people to pat their feet and dance to.
So what do you think? Do you think jazz has a chance?
